html:
SMTO-GML-0020 — Gmail OAuth state is invalid

GUID: 2a345dff-3661-4055-8e19-1cab5aead043
Slug: gmail-oauth-state-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The Google sign-in link or reply SMTO received doesn't belong to a sign-in that is still in progress. It may have expired, been used already, or come from an older attempt. Your Gmail account was not connected by this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, ask SMTO to connect your Gmail account again, and use only the new link it gives you. Each sign-in link works once, and older links stop working when a new attempt starts or the old one is finished.
  2. Finish the Google sign-in within 10 minutes of starting it. SMTO cancels unfinished sign-ins after 10 minutes for safety.
  3. Don't restart SMTO or edit the Gmail OAuth App entry on the Parameter Store page while you are signing in. Either one cancels the sign-in that is in progress.
  4. After Google sends you back, don't reload, bookmark or reopen that return page, and don't use an older Google link. Each return page works once, so loading it again sends an already-used reply that SMTO rejects.

What success looks like

  • The Google window says your account is connected and you can close it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they may need to check the return address set in the Gmail OAuth App entry. Never paste sign-in codes or links from Google into a conversation or screenshot.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail OAuth callback or start ticket was rejected because its state/ticket is malformed, unknown, already used or expired (10 minutes), the Gmail OAuth App parameter changed during the flow, or the redirect URI did not match.

What this means

  • OAuth state/ticket is malformed, absent, expired, reused, bound to a changed app revision or presented with a mismatched redirect URI. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth state/ticket is malformed, absent, expired, reused, bound to a changed app revision or presented with a mismatched redirect URI.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning flow and callback/app revision without reusing a consumed URL.

How to fix it

  • BrowserOAuth.launch_url/finish raise gmail_oauth_state_invalid for a non-ASCII or unknown ticket/state, an expired handshake (authorization_timeout maps here; lifetime 600 s), a redirect_uri mismatch, or when _app() sees a different updated_at/created_at on the Gmail OAuth App parameter. Pending handshakes are held in memory, so a Server restart also invalidates them. Start a new gmail.connect flow and complete it within 10 minutes without editing the OAuth App parameter.
  • Discard stale state and start a fresh supported OAuth flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh supported flow completes once with its matching current app and redirect.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
